content.text: {"utterance":"Nico, your risotto cook interests me, because I'd call that learning, yet notice what I'd need to see. If they swap ingredients successfully, I still don't know whether they understand why, or are copying a feel. So I'd ask: why did you add less stock? If they say \"it looked too wet,\" is that a reason? Maybe it is. A cook who can't explain in words but reliably adjusts seems to refute my criterion. So I'm unsure whether explanation is necessary, or only one test of reasons being present.","cites":["IR3","IR1"],"memory":"Claim: learning needs reasons, not just correct output. Nico's cook challenges whether verbal explanation is necessary. Live question: can a reliable adjustment, or a demonstration, count as giving a reason without words?"}
